en: Preface to the Ritual for the Practice of Western Rebirth The ritual for the practice of Western Rebirth is originally a Buddhist service performed by those who aspire to study the West (the Pure Land).

It was only after reading the *Miaozong* and *Yuanzhong* commentaries, as well as texts such as the *Ten Essentials of the Pure Land*, that I first came to understand that the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* contains two gates of practice: the gate of ten recitations and the gate of walking meditation.

The ritual procedures, the Forty-Eight Vows, and the chapters on the Nine Grades of Rebirth are all essential for the Pure Land. Profound faith and earnest aspiration do not arise except through these.
Therefore, I shall take these as my daily recitation and inform those of like mind that we together shall make them our warrant for rebirth in the Pure Land.
The *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* is the essential core of the hearts of all Buddhas and the family scripture of the Land of Bliss.
Its merit is inconceivable; therefore, those who hear this sūtra and uphold it shall all be protected and remembered by all the Buddhas.
At the moment of death, the holy assembly of Amitābha will appear before them to guide them. How much more so when many Buddhas exhort its upholding—how could one not recite it? (10)
The Dharma Gate of Mindfulness: The Great Vows of Amitābha are truly the guide to the Pure Land; they are indispensable for those who practice the path of purity.
Chan Master Chushih, whose Way was profound and virtues complete, maintained the ten recitations every morning without fail.

The "Ritual of Worship and Contemplation" and the "Entering into Meditation" were extracted from the liturgical procedures of Master Chishi. For practitioners who focus their cultivation, these are of the utmost urgency. Cultivate them!
In this state, without observing objects, the pure realm is vividly present; without engaging the mind, the true mind is fully revealed.

This may be called the marvelous achievement of seeing the Buddha and the wondrous secret of clarifying the mind. The Forty-Eight Vows and the Chapter on the Nine Grades are the causal mind of Dharmakara and the resultant virtue of Amitābha;
only by reading this can one finally understand the beginning and end of Amitābha’s cause and effect.
He does not abandon us, beings afflicted by suffering, but relies upon this name-holding;
in every thought-moment, one will surely be able to fully perfect the three kinds of provisions—faith, aspiration, and practice. The Western Return is not far off; it lies only herein.

All that has been stated above is the purport expounded by the various patriarchs, and is not mere speculative discourse. I only pray that all who see or hear this may give rise to resolute conviction.

Faith! Strive together to practice and uphold [the teachings], so that we may alike return to the vow of Amitābha, attain Buddhahood in this very life, and extensively deliver all sentient beings—all of this depends on this single undertaking;

it must not be delayed. This preface was respectfully written by the student Lian-si (Lian-si) Gu-kun at Shunjiang, while at the Tiantai Teaching and Contemplation Center, as he reverently burned forty-eight incense sticks from his arm as an offering to Amitābha Buddha. Prostrations. Dated the winter of the Guiyou year.
Preface to the Table of Contents for the Ritual Procedures for the Western Return;
Composed by the Repentance Master Ciyun for Distribution with the *Sūtra of Amitābha* and the Verses on Right Faith and Aspiration.
The Dharma Gate of the Ten Recitations for Rebirth in the Pure Land from the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* Spoken by the Buddha;

The Ritual for Paying Homage and Contemplating [Amitābha] from the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* Spoken by the Buddha (Appendix: The Great Repentance Text and the Ritual for Paying Homage to the Forty-Eight Vows).
The Ritual for Entering Contemplation and Performing Liturgy at Bedtime;
The Forty-Eight Vows Spoken by the Buddha in the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*;
The Nine Grades of Contemplation Chapter from the *Amitāyurdhyāna Sūtra*.

End of the Table of Contents for the Ritual Procedures for Paying Homage and Contemplating the Buddha Spoken by the Buddha in the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* and the Ritual Procedures for the Practice of Returning to the West.
The Ritual for the Practice of Western Repentance;
A Record Compiled by the Disciple of Śākyamuni Who Yearns for the West, Gu Kun;
Printed and Distributed by the Compassionate Cloud Repentance Master, together with Verses on Right Faith and the Making of Vows for the Amitābha Sūtra.

I prostrate to the Buddhas of the ten directions, to Amitābha, the most honored among the holy ones, to the Vaipulya Sūtras, the treasury of all Dharma-jewels, to Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and to the assembly of Bodhisattvas of the great earth.
With a heart of sincere faith, I have carved these woodblocks and printed them.
I shall have ten thousand copies each of the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* and the *Verses on Right Faith* produced; these shall be bestowed upon the fourfold assembly for their recitation and upholding.

The verses are intended to inspire faith, while the sūtra is intended to support their reading and chanting. If there are those who, during each day, recite at least three scrolls, [their merit shall be immeasurable].

Reciting one thousand and eighty [verses] per year amounts to ten thousand and eight hundred after ten years; how much more so for those who recite even more, and who thus accumulate such merit over many years?
They will naturally be born before the Buddha. Wherever these ten thousand scrolls of my sutras circulate, [may they flourish].
If even with the fewest possible, one person can recite and uphold [this] to be born in the Pure Land, I vow that by the power of this, I shall certainly be born in that land.
How much more so for many people! When a person passes away but the scripture remains, it is transmitted from one to another; this is called the "Inexhaustible Lamp."
Lamp after lamp illuminates one another, shattering the long night of birth and death and revealing the Buddha’s Bodhi.

All beings throughout space are born together within the Pure Land of Constant Quiescent Light. Taking this pure merit, I dedicate it to my sovereign and parents, and to the holy emperors of our land.
May the Holy Empress and those in holy positions each enjoy ten thousand years of benevolent longevity. May they protect and nourish all classes of sentient beings.
May my parents, kinsmen, and those who are neither enemies nor kin, all relying upon these supreme roots of goodness, be reborn together in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (Sukhāvatī).

The Essential Explanation states: This single practice of faith, aspiration, and the recitation of the Name does not involve worldly activities; it revolves perfectly through the five turbidities, relying solely on faith and entry.

It is a realm beyond the reach of discursive thought. Had the Original Teacher not come into this evil world to manifest the attainment of Bodhi, and had he not, with great wisdom and great compassion, seen this practice and taught these words, by what means could these sentient beings have received them?
Indeed it is so. Therefore, those who practice by reciting the name, whenever they chant the sutras, should first invoke:
"Namo to our Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha" (three times).
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on Amitābha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī, at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park... [up to] ...rejoicing.
Believing and accepting [this teaching], they prostrated and departed (end of sutra).
Recite the Mantra for Rebirth three times and dedicate the merit, saying:
"May this merit adorn the Buddha’s Pure Land, To repay in full the fourfold heavy恩情 (en) and debts of gratitude."
Descending to relieve the sufferings of the three evil realms, if there are those who see or hear [this], may they all resolve to attain Bodhicitta;
throughout this present physical existence, may they be born together in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Buddha said: "There are many bodhisattvas who wish to hear this sutra but are unable to obtain it. If there are sentient beings who hear..."
This sutra ensures that one shall never regress from the unsurpassed path.
Therefore, you should single-mindedly believe, accept, uphold, recite, explain, and practice it. Do not harbor doubts or uncertainties after my parinirvāṇa.
In future ages, when the Way of the sutras is about to perish, I shall, out of compassion and pity, specially preserve this sutra so that it remains for a hundred years.
Any sentient beings who encounter this sutra shall all attain liberation according to their respective wishes (from the *Daban*).

Formerly, during the Liang dynasty, there was the Dharma Master Daoren, who while practicing mindfulness of the Buddha at Mount Lu, suddenly dreamed that the river waters were overflowing and a multitude of people were boarding boats, saying they were traveling to the Western Land. Daoren said, "Daoren has spent his entire life practicing..."

The person from the west said, "I am ready to follow you. The man on the boat replied, "Although the Dharma Master’s exposition of the sutras is most profound, you have not yet recited the *Amitābha Sūtra* and the *Nianfo Sanzang Zhenyan* (Buddha-remembrance dharani). Your pure karma is not yet perfected; therefore, you may not go."

Ciyun said: Although the words and phrases of this scripture are concise, its meaning is identical to that of the Great Version. The Sages of antiquity responded to conditions through varying degrees of expansion and brevity;
herein, the primary and secondary [realms], the environment and its inhabitants, as well as the methods for vows and practice, are all fully present, surpassing other expositions.
The phrasing is concise while the meaning is vast; the merit of easy recitation is truly found herein. I ask that you first thoroughly examine the sections and divisions before reciting the text;
then, as the beginning and end will follow a logical order, your efforts will not be in vain.

If, perhaps during the clear morning or the quiet night, you withdraw your sight and hearing to sit upright, reciting with the mouth while the mind roams freely, allowing your spirit to dissolve into the profound depths, then all turbid burdens shall be cleansed away.
Do not be deluded regarding the pure realm; the Great Tongue [of the Buddha] exhorts you to uphold this.
Is it not so? The Dharma Gate of the Ten Recitations for Rebirth in the Pure Land, composed by the Great Master Ciyun of India.
Regarding the gate of ten recitations: every morning, having finished dressing, stand upright facing west with palms joined. Recite the name of Amitābha Buddha in a continuous voice;
one breath constitutes one recitation. In this manner, ten breaths constitute ten recitations.

Let the number of recitations follow the length of the breaths without limit; the measure is the exhaustion of the breath. The voice should be neither too high nor too low, neither too slow nor too hurried, but kept perfectly balanced.
In the midst [of this], the ten breaths are linked together so that the mind does not scatter; applying oneself with single-minded diligence is what is called the "ten recollections.
This is to bind the mind by means of the breath. Having performed these recollections, one makes a vow and dedicates the merit, saying:
I, disciple [Name], with single-minded devotion take refuge in Amitābha Buddha of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

May his light of purity illuminate me; may his compassionate vow embrace me. Now, with right mindfulness, I invoke the name of the Tathāgata for the duration of ten recitations, seeking rebirth in the Pure Land for the sake of the path to Bodhi.
According to the Buddha’s original vow: "If there are sentient beings who wish to be born in my land... [and so forth].

With a heart of faith and joy, even for ten recitations—if [the thought of Amida] should not arise, may I not attain perfect enlightenment, except in the case of those who have committed the five heinous crimes or slandered the True Dharma.
As I now reflect, throughout this present life, I have neither committed such heinous crimes nor slandered the Mahayana.
May these ten recitations enable me to enter the ocean of the Tathagata’s great vows; by riding upon the power of the Buddha’s compassion, may all my transgressions be extinguished and purified.
Through this increase, when one is about to die, one knows for oneself that the time has come;

the body is free from the suffering of illness, the mind is without attachment or longing, and the mind is neither inverted nor distracted, as if entering meditative absorption. Then the Buddha and the assembly of noble ones, holding golden platforms in their hands, come to welcome me.

In the space of a single thought-moment, one will be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss; upon the opening of the lotus flower, one shall behold the Buddha, immediately hear the Buddha-vehicle, suddenly awaken to the Buddha-wisdom, extensively deliver sentient beings, and fulfill the vow for Bodhi.

The Ritual for Paying Homage and Contemplating the Buddha of Infinite Life, Spoken by the Buddha (The full text of the visualization is included here for the convenience of beginners; the order of contemplation follows the sequence of the Triple Gem: Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha).
Compiled by the Disciple of the West, Gu Kunzun, based on ancient precedents.

(At that time, the Master [Gu] considered every word of the *Shorter Amitābha Sūtra* to be the true refuge of the practitioner and every word to be the practitioner’s wondrous contemplation. Since the unification of refuge and contemplation constitutes the practice of the sūtra, he subsequently compiled this ritual for receiving, upholding, and practicing it, and composed this preface himself for the sake of rebirth in the Pure Land.)

[The author] Yuan Shen greatly rejoiced in this. Therefore, following the *Hao-lüe* (Brief Essentials), he has complied with it and further compiled these rites for visualization (*li-xiang*). When a practitioner performs visualization, they first kneel before the Buddha, burn incense, join their palms, and say: (Note: The text provided ends here; the subsequent section contains the actual visualization liturgy.)

May these clouds of fragrant smoke pervade the worlds of the ten directions. May they make offerings to all Buddhas and to this Dharma that is difficult for the world to believe, as well as to all superior and virtuous persons.
May they universally perfume all sentient beings, causing them all to resolve upon Bodhicitta. (Then rise and prostrate to the Buddha.)
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate. To the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha, who, in this Sahā world of the five turbidities and evil age, preached the Dharma that is difficult to believe.
(Prostrate, while reciting the scripture.)

"Śāriputra, just as I now praise the inconceivable merits of all the Buddhas, so too do those Buddhas praise my own inconceivable merits, saying: 'The Buddha Śākyamuni has performed a most difficult and rare feat;

he was able to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi within the Sahā world-system, amidst the five corruptions of the evil age—the corruption of views, the corruption of afflictions, the corruption of sentient beings, the corruption of life, and the corruption of the kalpa—and for the sake of all sentient beings, he preaches this Dharma which is difficult for all the world to believe.
Śāriputra, you should know that in this world of the five corruptions, I have performed this difficult task, attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and preached it for the sake of the entire world."
"This Dharma is difficult to believe; it is exceedingly rare.

With single-minded devotion, prostrate yourself before the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the worlds of the ten directions, who extend their broad and long tongues to exhort and praise the Western Quarter (as described in the *Bai Xia Xiang Jing*).

"Śāriputra, just as I now praise the inconceivable benefits of the meritorious virtues of Amitābha Buddha, so too in the eastern direction there are Buddhas such as Akṣobhya Buddha, Merudhvaja Buddha, Mahāmeru Buddha, Meruprabhāsa Buddha, and Gadgadasvara Buddha.
These and other Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each from their own land, extend their broad and long tongues, covering the entire trichiliocosm, and speak words of truth:

'You sentient beings, you should believe this Sūtra on the Praise of Inconceivable Meritorious Virtues, which is protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas. "Śāriputra, in the southern world-system there are Buddhas such as Candrasūryapradīpa Buddha, Yaśaḥprabha Buddha, Mahārciskandha Buddha, Merupradīpa Buddha, and Anantavīrya Buddha."
Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each in their own land, extend their broad and long tongues, covering the entire trichiliocosm, and speak these words of truth:

"You sentient beings, you must believe this Sutra on the Praise of Inconceivable Merit, which is protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas. Śāriputra, in the western world there are the Buddha Amitāyus, the Buddha Amitākṣa, the Buddha Amitadhvaja, the Buddha Mahāprabha, the Buddha Mahārcis, the Buddha Ratnākṣa, the Buddha Viśuddhaprabha, and others as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

Each in their own land extends their broad and long tongues, covering the entire trichiliocosm, and speaks these words of truth: "You sentient beings, you must believe this praise of inconceivable..."

The Sutra on the Merits of Contemplation Protected by All Buddhas. Śāriputra, in the world-systems of the northern direction, there are the Buddha Flame Shoulder, the Buddha Most Victorious Sound, the Buddha Unassailable, the Buddha Sun-Born, the Buddha Net-Luminosity, and others such as these—Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.

Each, in his own land, extends his broad and long tongue until it completely covers the trichiliocosm, and speaks words of truth, saying: "You sentient beings, you should believe this Sutra on the Merits of Contemplation Protected by All Buddhas.

Śāriputra, in the world-systems of the lower direction, there are the Buddha Lion, the Buddha Renowned Name, the Buddha Named Light, the Buddha Dharma, the Buddha Dharma Banner, the Buddha Upholder of Dharma, and others such as these—Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. Each, in his own land...

That land produces the mark of the broad and long tongue, which completely covers the trichiliocosm. He speaks words of truth: "You sentient beings, you should believe this Sutra on the Praise of the Inconceivable Merit Protected and Mindfully Kept by All Buddhas."

Śāriputra, in the worlds above there are Buddhas such as Brahmā-voice Buddha, Constellation King Buddha, Fragrance Supreme Buddha, Fragrant Light Buddha, Great Flame Shoulder Buddha, Adorned Body with Variegated Jewel Flower Buddha, Śāla Tree King Buddha, Jewel Flower Virtue Buddha, Seeing All Meanings Buddha, and Tathāgata Like Mount Sumeru.

These and other Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each from their respective lands, extend their broad and long tongues until they completely cover the trichiliocosm, and speak these words of truth: "You sentient beings..."
One should believe in this *Sūtra on the Praise of the Inconceivable Merit and the Protection and Mindfulness of All Buddhas*.

With single-minded devotion, prostrate to Amitābha Buddha in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, whose light and lifespan are immeasurable, who universally gathers in all living beings, and who is described in the *Sūtra* as follows:
[prostrate below while visualizing].

“Śāriputra, what do you think? For that reason, I call that Buddha Amitābha. Śāriputra, the light of that Buddha is immeasurable; it illuminates the lands of the ten directions without obstruction. For this reason, he is called Amitābha.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, the lifespan of that Buddha, as well as that of his people, is immeasurable and boundless asaṃkhyeya kalpas. Therefore, he is named Amitāyus. Śāriputra, since Amitābha Buddha attained Buddhahood, ten kalpas have passed until now.”
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, who, when one holds His name,
will guide one at the moment of death (as described in the *Sūtra on Visualizing the Buddha*).
"Śāriputra, one cannot attain birth in that land through small roots of goodness or causes and conditions of merit.

Śāriputra, if there are good men or good women who, upon hearing the name of Amitābha Buddha, hold fast to it—whether for one day, two days, three days, four days, five days, six days, or seven days—with single-mindedness and without distraction, then at the time of their death, Amitābha Buddha, together with a multitude of holy beings, will appear before them.

At the moment of death, such a person’s mind will not be inverted, and they will immediately attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitābha Buddha. Śāriputra, because I see this benefit, I speak these words: if there are sentient beings who hear this teaching, they should make a vow to be born there."
To the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the Western Quarter, I prostrate with single-minded devotion. May all beings—past, present, and future—be enabled to be reborn there.
To Amitābha Buddha, [I prostrate]. (As described in the *Bai-xia-xiang-jing*):

"Śāriputra, if there are those who have already made a vow, are now making a vow, or shall make a vow, desiring to be born in the land of Amitābha Buddha, all such persons shall attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

Whether they have already been born, are currently being born, or will be born in that land—for this reason, Śāriputra, all sons and daughters of good family who possess faith should make a vow to be born in that land.
With single-minded devotion, they should prostrate and praise the *Sūtra on the Inconceivable Merit Admired and Protected by All Buddhas*.
And all the honored Dharmas of the ten directions and the three periods of time (according to the *Bai-xia-xiang-jing*):
"Śāriputra, what do you think? For what reason is this called the *Sūtra Protected and Mindfully Kept by All Buddhas*?

Śāriputra, if there are good men or good women who hear this sūtra and receive and uphold it, as well as those who hear the names of the Buddhas—all these good men and good women shall be protected and mindfully kept by all the Buddhas, and they shall all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Therefore, Śāriputra, you all..."
You should faithfully accept my words, as well as those spoken by all the Buddhas.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate yourself before the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, all the superior and virtuous beings,
and the assembly of pure Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas like a great ocean (as described in the Sutra).

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, that Buddha has immeasurable and boundless śrāvaka disciples, all of whom are arhats, beyond what can be known by calculation. The assembly of bodhisattvas is likewise so. Śāriputra, such is that Buddha’s land."

They have thus accomplished the adornment of such meritorious qualities. Furthermore, Śāriputra, those beings who are born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss are all *avaivartika* (non-retrogressive). Among them, there are many who are in their final birth before Buddhahood (*ekajātipratibaddha*);

their number is so vast that it cannot be known by calculation, but can only be described as immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*). Śāriputra, when sentient beings hear this, they should make a vow to be born in that land. Why is this? Because they will be able to associate with such supreme and virtuous persons.
Gathering together in one place, they single-mindedly prostrate themselves.
At the foot of a tree in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, hearing the sounds [of the birds], they maintain right mindfulness.
All the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas... (The *Bai-xia-xiang-jing* states).

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that land there are always various wonderful birds of diverse colors: white cranes, peacocks, parrots, śāris, kalaviṅkas, and jīvañjīvakas. These many birds, throughout the six periods of day and night, produce harmonious and elegant sounds.

Those sounds expound upon the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path, and such dharmas as these. When the sentient beings of that land hear these sounds, they all recollect the Buddha, recollect the Dharma, and recollect the Saṃgha. Śāriputra..."

Do not think that these birds are actually born as a result of karmic retribution. Why is this? In that Buddha-land, Śāriputra, there are no three evil realms; indeed, even the names of the evil realms do not exist there, let alone their actual presence.

These various birds are all transformations produced by Amitābha Buddha, intended to cause the sounds of the Dharma to flow forth. Śāriputra, when the gentle breeze stirs the trees made of various jewels and the jeweled nets in that Buddha-land, they produce subtle and wondrous sounds like a hundred thousand kinds of music playing simultaneously.

Those who hear these sounds naturally give rise to thoughts of mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, and mindfulness of the Saṅgha. Śāriputra, that Buddha-land is thus adorned with such meritorious qualities.

With single-minded devotion, prostrate and pay homage to the Buddhas in the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the Western Quarter, upon the ground of pure gold, where they present abundant flowers as offerings;
to all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas (*as described in the scripture below*).

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that Buddha-land celestial music constantly plays; the ground is made of gold, and throughout the six periods of day and night, it rains *mandārava* flowers. The sentient beings of that land always at dawn each take a robe-sack filled with various wonderful flowers."

He makes offerings to ten trillion buddhas in other directions; then, at the time of the meal, he returns to his own land to eat and practice walking meditation. Śāriputra, the Land of Ultimate Bliss is thus adorned with such meritorious qualities.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas within the precious pavilions in the lotus ponds of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss (as described in the Sūtra).

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, in the Land of Ultimate Bliss there are ponds made of the seven treasures, filled with water possessing the eight meritorious qualities. The bottoms of these ponds are entirely covered with golden sand. The steps and walkways on their four sides are composed of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal.

Above them are pavilions, likewise adorned with gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, *śaṅkha-śilā* (conch-shell stone), red pearls, and *musāragalva* (agate). Within the ponds, lotus flowers are as large as chariot wheels; those that are blue emit a blue light, those that are yellow emit a yellow light, those that are red emit a red light, and those that are white emit a white light—all of them subtle, wondrous, fragrant, and pure.
Śāriputra, the Land of Ultimate Bliss is thus accomplished with such meritorious adornments."
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, where there are no manifold sufferings and one experiences only various joys.
To all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas (prostrate as prescribed in the sutra).

At that time, the Buddha addressed the Elder Śāriputra: "From here, to the west, beyond a hundred thousand koṭis of buddha-fields, there is a world named Sukhāvatī. In that land there is a Buddha named Amitābha, who is currently dwelling and preaching the Dharma. Śāriputra,..."
For what reason is that land named Sukhāvatī? Because the sentient beings of that country have no manifold sufferings and experience only various joys, it is therefore called Sukhāvatī.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, the land of Sukhāvatī is surrounded on all sides by sevenfold railings, sevenfold nets, and sevenfold rows of trees, all made of the four jewels; for this reason, that country is named Sukhāvatī.

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to Mañjuśrī and Maitreya, all the great Bodhisattvas, Śāriputra and the other great venerable ones, and all the holy assemblies of the ten directions and the three periods of time. (As described in the scripture, perform prostrations while visualizing.)
Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus.

All were great arhats, renowned among the multitude, including the elders Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Mahākātyāyana, Mahākauṣṭhila, Revata, Cūḍapanthaka, Nanda, Ānanda, Rāhula, Gavāmpati, and Piṇḍola.

Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Ānanda, Rāhula, Revata, Kapphiṇa, Kālodayin, Mahākapphiṇa, Bakula, Aniruddha, and other such great disciples, together with the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī.
The Bodhisattva Ajita, the Bodhisattva Gandhahasti, the Bodhisattva Nityodyukta, and other such great bodhisattvas, together with Śakra-devānām-indra and an immeasurable assembly of devas.
Having completed the ritual visualization, kneel and recite one scroll of the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* and the *Nianfo Sanqianwen Zhenzhou* three times.
Then offer this praise: The body of Amitābha Buddha is golden in color; His marks and signs and radiant light are peerless. His white tuft curls like five Mount Sumerus;
His deep blue eyes are as clear as the four great oceans. Within his light, countless billions of transformation Buddhas appear, And hosts of transformed Bodhisattvas likewise...
Boundless! Through forty-eight vows, he delivers sentient beings; those of the nine grades are all enabled to ascend to the other shore.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, Greatly Compassionate and Greatly Merciful. (Recite the name of the Buddha as many times as your strength permits, then cease.)
Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Homage to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva.
Homage to the assembly of Bodhisattvas of the Pure Great Ocean (recite each ten times). Having finished the recitation, perform the dedication and make the vow, saying:
The disciple recites the name of Amitābha, the Buddha of True Merit;
I pray only that you will compassionately grant your acceptance, Witnessing my repentance and my aspirations.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past Arise entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
I now repent of all that has arisen from my body, speech, and mind. May I,
at the time when my life is about to end, Have all obstacles completely removed,
And behold that Buddha Amitābha face-to-face, Thereby attaining rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

I now dedicate all the roots of goodness I have cultivated, in their entirety, universally, wishing that all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm may together be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
I take refuge in the Buddha. May all sentient beings realize the Great Way and give rise to the unsurpassed mind.
Taking refuge in the Dharma, may all sentient beings enter deeply into the treasury of the scriptures, their wisdom as vast as the ocean.
Taking refuge in the Sangha, may all sentient beings preside over the great assembly, free from all obstacles.
Homage to the Assembly of Sages:

Text for Great Repentance (To be added after the phrase "Greatly Compassionate Amitābha Buddha of the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Read this text first, and then recite the Buddha's name; it may also be omitted).
I, disciple [Name], repent with a sincere heart. May the Buddhas of the ten directions truly see and know me and the assembly.
Birth is by nature pure; it is the dwelling place of all Buddhas, called the Constantly Quiescent Light (*nitya-prabhāsvara*).
It pervades every moment and all phenomena, yet I do not understand this. I falsely conceive of a self and persons, giving rise to discrimination within the equal Dharma.

Within the pure mind, I produce defiled attachments. Because of such inversion, through the causes and conditions of the five desires, I circulate through birth and death. Thus it is said in the *Sūtra*: [text continues].
Transmigrating through the three realms, they remain bound within this continuity, never contemplating the time of liberation. Furthermore, while therein, they commit the most extreme evil karmas:

the four grave offenses and the five heinous crimes; they become icchantikas, slandering and reviling the Mahāyāna; they defame and destroy the Triple Gem; they deny the existence of all Buddhas; they sever their study of Prajñāpāramitā;

they misappropriate the property of the Sangha from the ten directions and the property of Buddha-stūpas; they defile those who practice the pure life (brahmacarya); and they habitually associate with and adopt evil dharmas.

Regarding those who break the precepts, they further praise and protect one another. These practitioners of the Three Vehicles sow seeds of slander within, while outwardly concealing their faults and manifesting dignified deportment.
They constantly use the five forms of deviance to solicit the four requisites, preaching the Dharma with impurity and instructing others in what is contrary to the Vinaya.

Having left the household life because of the Buddha, they instead destroy the Buddha-dharma and act in opposition to their teachers and elders. Despite being instructed according to the Dharma, they indulge freely in greed and anger, lacking any sense of shame or remorse.
Due to these causes and conditions, by the power of their various evil karmas, at the end of their lives they shall fall into the Avīci Hell.
The fierce flames blaze intensely; one undergoes immeasurable suffering for thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, with no prospect of liberation.
Only now do I begin to realize this, giving rise to great shame and remorse, and great fear. The World-Honored Ones of the ten directions and Amitābha Buddha have long since [regarded me].
He gave rise to a heart of great compassion. Throughout incalculable eons, for the sake of delivering me, he cultivated the bodhisattva path, not sparing even his own body or life.
Now that he has attained Buddhahood, his great compassion is fully perfected; he is truly able to provide protection and salvation for all. Yet now, I have committed evil.
I shall surely fall into the three miserable realms. I pray that you will arouse compassion and accept my repentance, so that my grave offenses may be extinguished and all evils eliminated.
May the causes for rebirth in this Sahā world be forever exhausted, and may I be born, as I wish, in the pure lands of the Buddhas. At the time of my death—
All is without obstruction. Having completed my repentance, my six faculties and three karmas are pure and free from blemish. The roots of goodness I have cultivated are likewise entirely pure;
I dedicate them all to adorn the Pure Land, so that I and all sentient beings may together be born in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (An-yang).
I pray that Amitābha Buddha will constantly come to protect and sustain me, causing my roots of goodness to increase and manifest before me, so that I do not lose the pure cause.

At the time of my death, may my body and mind remain in right mindfulness, with sight and hearing clear and distinct; may I behold Amitābha face-to-face, as he, together with the assembly of holy ones, holds a lotus pedestal in his hand to welcome and lead me forth.
In a single kṣaṇa, may I be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and upon the opening of the flower, may I behold him.
The Buddha immediately heard the Buddha-vehicle and suddenly opened the Buddha-wisdom, extensively delivering sentient beings and fulfilling his bodhi-vow.
Having finished repenting and making vows, he took refuge in and paid homage to Amitābha Buddha and all the Triple Gem.
The Ritual for the Forty-Eight Vows (to be performed at any time, morning or evening).

With single-minded devotion, prostrate before Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss—the Greatly Compassionate, Greatly Benevolent, Teacher who Guides and Welcomes, endowed with great vows and great power.

(First prostration: silently recite the first vow. Second prostration: silently recite the second vow. Continue in this manner until the forty-eighth prostration, silently reciting the forty-eighth vow.)
The Eight Vows. For those unable to recite the vows, it is also permissible to perform forty-eight prostrations while keeping count.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate and pay homage to the World-Honored One Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the Pure Great Ocean of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
(Three prostrations for each verse) May these merits adorn the Buddha’s Pure Land; Above, to repay the fourfold heavy恩情 (en);
Below, to relieve the suffering of the three paths. Should there be any who see or hear this, May they all resolve to attain Bodhicitta.
Exhausting this present retribution-body, may we be born together in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
*Procedure for Contemplation and Recitation upon Entering Sleep* Compiled Briefly by the Disciple of the Western Paradise, Gu Kunzun.

(The practitioner should know that the *Sūtra on the Visualization of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life* states: The Buddha addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī: "Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this well. I shall now, for your sake, analyze and explain the method for eliminating suffering and affliction.

You should remember and uphold it, and extensively analyze and explain it for the great assembly. Since we have been moved by the Buddha’s kindness and received this Dharma-gate, we should first perform such prostrations.)
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage. To the World-Honored One of this Sahā world, who analytically explains the Dharma for removing suffering and affliction:
our Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha. (Bowing down, recite the verse:)

The nature of the worshiper and the object of worship is empty and tranquil; the mutual resonance of cause and response is inconceivable. My place of practice is like a celestial jewel, within which the shadow of Śākyamuni Tathāgata appears. The shadow of my own body now appears before the Tathāgata, as I seek to transcend suffering by prostrating at his feet.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate in homage. In the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, dwelling upon the waters of a lotus pond, he abides upon a precious lotus flower.

He manifests a body sixteen feet tall, his form the color of pure gold, with a halo of light shining through with perfect clarity. Within that halo are immeasurable transformation Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and Amitābha Buddha.
(The verse for visualization says:)

The nature of both the worshiper and the object of worship is empty and quiescent; the resonance between cause and response is inconceivable. This site of my practice is like a jewel of Indra, within which the reflection of Amitābha Buddha appears. My own form and shadow appear before Amitābha, seeking rebirth there as I prostrate at his feet.
With single-minded devotion, pay homage to the Buddha Standing with a Celestial Crown upon the waters of the pond in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss,
together with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara (in the verse of visualization, change "Avalokiteśvara" to "the manifestation of Avalokiteśvara").
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta (in the verse of visualization, change "Mahāsthāmaprāpta" to "Śrīprabhāsa"),
who dwells upon the waters of the pond in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, with a jeweled vase atop his uṣṇīṣa.

With single-minded devotion, prostrate yourself. For those who are born in the highest grade of the highest level in the Land of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*), who recite and study, cultivate loving-kindness, and fully develop the three minds—bow down to all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas (when bowing, one should visualize the text of this specific chapter; if one cannot visualize the scripture, it is sufficient to direct one’s heart with utmost sincerity toward them).

With single-minded devotion, I prostrate. To those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are born by the middle grade of the superior class in the World of Ultimate Bliss, who have realized the primary meaning, and whose minds are not shaken—[I pay homage].

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage. Regarding those born in the highest grade of the lower level in the World of Ultimate Bliss: it is sufficient for them merely to give rise to the unsurpassed, pure mind of the Way.
This applies to all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage. To those who are born in the middle grade of the superior rebirth in the world of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*), who practice all the precepts and are free from all faults and afflictions, and to all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.

With single-minded devotion, pay homage! Among those born by the middle grade in the world of Ultimate Bliss, for one day and one night, they maintain the precepts and dignified deportment, together with all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage. To those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are born into the middle grade of rebirth in the world of Ultimate Bliss, who filially support their parents, and who practice worldly benevolence and compassion.

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage. In the World of Ultimate Bliss, those of the highest rank of the lower grade are born; though they have many evil reputations, the Buddha and the three sages come to comfort and welcome them, as do the various Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.

With single-minded devotion, I prostrate. In the lower-middle grade of rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, though one has violated the precepts, upon hearing of the Buddha, the fires are extinguished and the Sage appears.
All the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas—

With single-minded devotion, prostrate in homage. Even those of the lowest of the low grades reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss who have committed heinous crimes may transcend [suffering] by invoking the Buddha’s name ten times.
Homage to all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
Having paid homage and contemplated thus, kneel long with palms joined and recite the "Chapter on the Nine Grades of Contemplation" from the *Buddhabhāṣita Aparimitāyur-jñāna-sūtra*.
Recite until reaching the passage: "One shall sit at the site of enlightenment and be born into the family of all Buddhas. With a sincere mind and all one's strength, maintain mindfulness.
Namo Amitābha Buddha (ten breaths).
Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Namo Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva.
Namo to the Bodhisattvas of the Pure Great Ocean Assembly (ten recitations each).
With a sincere heart, one makes this vow, saying:

"I, disciple [Name], am currently an ordinary person in the cycle of birth and death. My karmic obstructions are deep and heavy; I transmigrate through the six realms of existence, suffering without end."

It may be said: Now that I have encountered a spiritual friend and been able to hear the name of Amitābha Buddha and the merits of his original vows, I shall single-mindedly recite it and pray for rebirth in his land.
I pray that the Buddha, out of compassion, will not abandon me, but will take pity on me and receive me into his grace.

This disciple, [Name], does not recognize the Buddha’s body, its marks and signs, or its radiance; I pray that the Buddha will manifest himself so that I may behold him, as well as Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
May all the assemblies of Bodhisattvas in that world—its pure adornments, radiant splendors, wondrous signs, and so forth—be clearly perceived by me.
(Having prostrated three times before the Buddha, one returns to the quarters to rest.)
The Sutra of Immeasurable Life Spoken by the Buddha:
The Forty-eight Vows, translated by Kang Sengkai during the Cao Wei dynasty.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda: "In the remote past, incalculable eons ago, the Buddha Lokeśvararāja appeared in the world."

In the *Contemplation Sūtra on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life*, within the chapter on the nine grades of contemplation, the World-Honored One (up to the realm of emptiness) praised them, saying: "They shall certainly and inevitably attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Kangārāśa of the Western Regions during the Liu Song dynasty.
The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī: "If you wish to give rise to a sincere mind directed toward the Western Quarter, you should first contemplate the image one zhang and six chi in height...
[until] becoming their supreme friends; you shall sit at the site of enlightenment and be born into the family of all Buddhas."
In the first year of the Tongzhi era, while I was at Huiji Temple on Mount Foding, I read the *Ten Essentials of the Pure Land*.

Upon reaching the *Treatise on the King of Jewels*, I learned that when Master Zhiyi was approaching his death, he instructed that the Forty-eight Vows and the chapter on the Nine Grades of Contemplation be recited for him.
Considering that Master Zhiyi was the Śākyamuni of this eastern land, that he should have had these recited at the moment of his passing—how could they not be of the utmost importance?

Statement: Because of this, I have read it thoroughly and shall offer it as my daily practice. I believe that Amitābha’s power of vows universally encompasses the nine realms of existence entirely thanks to the Great Master’s dissemination of the teachings.
I, Gu Kun, a successor in the lineage of the Dharma, respectfully burn nine incense sticks from my arm and record this with reverence.
Regarding the ritual for bowing and visualization according to the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* (The Smaller Sukhāvatī-vyūha): those who are able to perform the visualization should follow the full ritual;

those who cannot should simply follow this direct method of prostration, as the merit will be no different. When performing prostrations, first kneel before the Buddha and burn incense, then join [the palms].
[The Master] clasps his hands and says:

"May these clouds of incense smoke pervade the worlds of the ten directions, making offerings to all Buddhas, to the Dharma that is difficult for the world to believe, and to all those who are supreme and virtuous.
May they universally permeate all sentient beings, causing them all to resolve upon Bodhicitta. (Then he rises.)
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage. To our Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha, who in this Sahā world of the five turbidities and evil age preaches the Dharma that is difficult to believe;

with single-minded devotion, I pay homage. To those throughout the worlds of the ten directions who extend their broad and long tongues to exhort and praise the West, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to all Buddhas. To Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, whose light and lifespan are immeasurable, who universally gathers in all sentient beings.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, who, when one holds His name, guides them at the moment of death.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss; now I make this vow that all may be led to be reborn there. Amitābha.
Homage to the Buddha.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage and praise the *Sūtra on the Merit of Inconceivable Virtue, Protected and Mindfully Sustained by All Buddhas*,
as well as all the Honored Dharmas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the World of Ultimate Bliss in the western quarter, to Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, to all the supreme and virtuous ones,
and to the assembly of pure Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas as vast as the great ocean.

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who, beneath the trees in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, hear the sounds of the spiritual birds and maintain right mindfulness;
with single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all the Bodhisattvas who offer abundant flowers to the Buddhas upon the golden ground of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage with one-pointed mind to all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas within the precious pavilions in the lotus ponds of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, where there are no manifold sufferings and only various joys are experienced,
and to all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to Mañjuśrī and Maitreya, all the great bodhisattvas, Śāriputra and the other great venerable ones,
and all the holy assemblies of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Kneeling, recite one scroll of the *Amitābha Sūtra* and the *Nien-fo San-ch'ien Chou* (Buddha-Recitation Three-Thousand-Verses Dharani) three times. Then offer praise, saying:
The body of Amitābha Buddha is golden in color; His marks and signs and radiance are peerless.
His white tuft curls like five Mount Sumerus; His deep blue eyes are as clear as the four great oceans.
Within the light, countless billions of transformation Buddhas appear, and the assembly of transformed Bodhisattvas is likewise boundless.
Through the Forty-eight Vows, they deliver all sentient beings, causing those of the nine grades to ascend together to the other shore.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, Greatly Compassionate and Greatly Merciful. (Recite the Buddha’s name as much as your strength permits, then cease.)
Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Homage to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva.
Homage to the assembly of Bodhisattvas of the Pure Great Ocean (recite each ten times). Having finished the recitation, perform the dedication and make this vow:
The disciple recites the name of Amitābha, the Buddha of True Merit;
I pray only that you will compassionately grant your protection and acceptance, witnessing my repentance and my aspirations.
All the various evil karmas I have created in the past arose entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind, I now repent it all. May I,
when the time comes for my life to end, Have all obstacles completely removed,
And behold that Buddha Amitābha face-to-face, Thereby attaining rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
All the roots of goodness that I have now cultivated, I dedicate them all entirely,
universally vowing that all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm may together be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Taking refuge in the Buddha, I vow that all sentient beings shall realize the Great Way and give rise to the unsurpassed mind.
Taking refuge in the Dharma, may all beings enter deeply into the treasury of the scriptures, their wisdom as vast as the ocean.
Taking refuge in the Sangha, may all beings lead and harmonize the great assembly, free from all hindrances.
Homage to the Noble Assembly.
The Order of Succession for the Eighteen Worthies of Donglin:
Dharma Master Huiyuan, Dharma Master Huiying, Dharma Master Huichi,
Dharma Master Daosheng, Dharma Master Tanshun, and Dharma Master Sengrui.
Dharma Master Tanyang, Dharma Master Daobing, Dharma Master Tanshen, Dharma Master Daojing,
Dharma Master Jiaoming, and Dharma Master Jiaxian (who was the Venerable Buddhabhadra),
along with Liu Chengzhi, Zhang Ye, and Zhou Xuzhi.
Zhang Quan, Zhong Bing, Lei Cizong, and Dharma Master Huiyuan greatly opened the Lotus School (Lotus Sect).
As it fundamentally followed the scriptural teachings, they are called the first patriarchs who uniquely proclaimed it;
they are named the foremost sages. The twelfth was the Venerable Buddhabhadra, who was the distant ancestor that propagated the practice of mindfulness of the Buddha.

Samādhi. Regarding the fact that those who joined the society twenty-seven years later are now worshipped as the first patriarchs of the Pure Land school, and that it is said these distant ancestors were the teachers who transmitted the *nien-fo* samādhi—this is an extreme error. This is detailed in the *Fozu Tongji*.
I have respectfully set forth the ritual for venerating the patriarchs of the Lotus School below, so that it may be followed in practice. [The daily recitation] on the new and full moon:
[Having finished,] join the palms and say:
"I prostrate to the successive patriarchs of India and China."
The Great Spiritual Friends who propagated the teachings and precepts throughout the world (of the Lotus School):
The First Patriarch, Grand Master Huiyuan of Mount Lu (passed into rebirth on the sixth day of the eighth month);
The Second Patriarch, Grand Master Shandao of Guangming (unverified; the birthday of Amitābha Buddha should be observed as his anniversary).
The Third Patriarch, Grand Master Banzhou Chengyuan (reborn on the nineteenth day of the seventh month);
the Fourth Patriarch, Grand Master Wuhui Fazhao (reborn on the first day of the twelfth month);
and the Fifth Patriarch, Grand Master Taiyan Shaokang (reborn on the third day of the tenth month).
The Sixth Patriarch, Great Master Yongming Yijue (passed away on the twenty-sixth day of the second month);
the Seventh Patriarch, Great Master Zhaoking Shengchang (passed away on the twelfth day of the first month);
the Eighth Patriarch, Great Master Yunqi Lianchi (passed away on the second day of the seventh month).
The Ninth Patriarch, Grand Master Ouyi of Lingfeng (passed away on the twenty-first day of the first month);
the Tenth Patriarch, Grand Master Siqu of Fantian (passed away on the fourteenth day of the fourth month);
the Eleventh Patriarch, Grand Master Chewu of Zifú (passed away on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month).
The Ritual for Returning to the West, Following the Practice of the Great Dharma Masters of the Lotus Societies of Past and Present (Concluded).
In the summer of the ninth year of the Guangxu era, Gu Kun, a student of Western learning from Lianxi, respectfully records this postscript to the *Sūtra on Amitābha* Spoken by the Buddha.
Regarding the *Yuanzhong chao*, it states: "This is precisely the secret treasury of the three virtues; it is perfectly all-encompassing."
If expanded, it encompasses the entire Dharma-realm: one is all. If condensed, it is subsumed within a single sutra: all is one.
One who can understand it thus may rightly say that the single sutra of Amitābha fills the Dharma-realm, and that the Dharma-realms of the ten directions all possess this sutra.
Those who receive and uphold it shall be protected and remembered by all Buddhas; as for that which they protect and remember—
This is where one seeks the Pure Land. One must urgently recite [the name], so that by this merit, one may swiftly proceed to the Western Quarter.
In the study and recitation of the Mahāyāna, nothing surpasses this. As for the gate of the ten recitations, Amitābha established his vows to guide those who uphold them;
how could one fail to follow them? Every morning, one should recite while facing west. Master Chu said: "Only when a single region is pure is it truly a pure land."
The ten recitations are pure; the mind is true, and every thought is true. This deeply captures the profound essence of the ten recitations facing west.

Therefore, Lingfeng praised Chushih as being the very perfect enlightenment of Amitābha. For this reason, even if a practitioner of the Nembutsu attains single-mindedness and non-distraction, this practice must never be abandoned.
If this practice is once abandoned, one's faith and vow will not be earnest, and [one will fail to] proceed.

It is difficult to attain birth [in the Pure Land]. Therefore, the *Yaojie* (Essential Explanation) states: "If one lacks faith and aspiration, even if one recites the Name until it is as windproof as not being blown by the wind and as water-proof as not being soaked by rain, there is still no principle by which birth can be attained.
Regarding the two principles (*er yi*), they consist in the operation of the utmost sincerity of the three karmas.
When one faces the wondrous realm of the West, the Buddha and the mind appear vividly before one; self and other are not separated.

Thus, it is clearly understood that "this mind creates the Buddha" and "this mind is the Buddha. If one can follow this principle, then even if one's faith and aspiration were not originally deep, they will naturally become so.
The Preface to *Essential Readings for the Lotus School* states: "From what source do the merits of the Name originate?
They arise from the adornment of the Sixty-Eight Great Vows and the accomplishment of the Compassionate Heart of the Nine Grades.

Therefore, those who single-mindedly uphold the Name should thoroughly study these two scriptural passages; firm faith and aspiration depend entirely upon them. Thus did Master Lianxi [Zhiyuan] [state].
With a heart of utmost sincerity, this single work was compiled; it may truly be said to accord with both principle and capacity, being perfect in beauty and excellence.

Its preface is a marvelous proclamation and an ultimate discourse, precise and thorough in its penetration. This could not have been achieved without attaining samādhi or the secret empowerment of the Buddhas.
To briefly cite from the subsequent text: "The cause and fruition of Amitābha never abandon us, the suffering sentient beings, from beginning to end," and so forth.
"This name-holding practice; in every thought-moment, one will surely be able to fully perfect the three kinds of provisions: faith, aspiration, and practice. How true these words are!
Without having grasped the very marrow of the Pure Land school, it would indeed be difficult to achieve such realization. Upon my first reading, it was as if I had discovered a treasure;

the more I read, the deeper it became, and the more I reflected, the more wondrous it grew. I feel deep shame at the heaviness of my own defilements—how fortunate I am to have heard this and gained such benefit.

I am deeply grateful; my thanks are beyond measure. Only now do I realize that my previous practice of the Name was entirely devoid of faith and aspiration, being nothing more than the suppression of deluded thoughts.
For this reason, I frequently changed the titles of my recitations, seeking instead something profound and subtle. Thus, Master Jianmi said:
"Without having attained pure faith and pure aspiration, how can one shoulder the Great Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the ten directions and the three periods of time?"
I only pray that those who cultivate the karma of purity will exert all their strength to follow this ritual practice;

then their faith and aspiration will surely become firm, their western journey home will surely be secure, seeing the Buddha will not be difficult, and the salvation of sentient beings will likewise be vast.

On a summer day in the Jiashu year of the Tongzhi era, the student Fanghui respectfully burned forty-eight incense sticks from his own arm as an offering to the Dharma-gate of the Pure Land, bowing his head in reverence and recording this.
The scholar Wei Xia respectfully carved three incense offerings on his arm to make an offering to the Buddha and made this vow:
"By these merits, may I swiftly go to the Land of Ultimate Bliss to behold Amitābha face-to-face, and extensively deliver all beings."
